newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Regent Pacific to issue shares in Hong Kong IPO.
newsitem.headline: Regent Pacific to issue shares in Hong Kong IPO.

text.p: Hong Kong-based Regent Pacific Group Ltd announced on Monday plans to expand its eastern European corporate finance operations and acquire an interest in a European finance house following its upcoming share issue.
Earlier, the fund management firm said it expected to raise HK$447 million ($58 million) through an offering of 170.51 million shares priced at HK$2.62 each (US$0.34) each.
Group director Peter Everington said 42.63 million new shares would be listed locally and 127.88 million shares had already been placed internationally.

"Our growth strategy is focused on the expansion of our fund management business, in particular in Russia and Eastern Europe, as well as on the broadening of our client base," Everington told a news conference.
"We will also continue to develop our corporate finance and brokerage capabilities in eastern Europe," he said.
The firm plans to use HK$116-$155 million to expand its eastern European corporate finance capability, and HK$116 million to acquire an interest in a European finance house, Everington said.
The total 170.5 million shares on offer represent about 18 percent of the group's enlarged issued share capital.

In addition, Regent Pacific has granted underwriters an over-allotment option which would require the company to issue up to a total 31 million additional shares to cover over-allocations or over-subscriptions.
The group's management and staff, who formerly held 41 percent of Regent Pacific, will remain its main shareholders with a stake of about 33 percent after the offer's completion.
The IPO will run from Tuesday to Friday. Dealing of shares on the local stock exchange is expected to start on May 19.

Based on an estimated net profit of HK$235 million for the year to March 31, the issue price represents a price-to-earnings ratio of 9.92 times on a weighted average basis, and 9.89 times on a pro-forma fully-diluted basis, Everington said.
Net profit is forecast at HK$200 million for the six months to September 30, 1997, he added.

The group, set up in 1990, provides investment management and advisory services in emerging markets to institutional and professional investors worldwide. It had about US$1.77 billion worth of assets under management as at February 28.
Net proceeds from the offer are estimated at HK$413.8 million if the over-allotment option is not exercised, and HK$493 million if it is exercised in full.
Nomura International (Hong Kong) Ltd is the sponsor and lead manager for the placement and IPO.
The company concentrates on fund management, corporate finance, corporate investment and security brokerage.
Apart from its headquarters in Hong Kong, Regent Pacific has offices in London, Sydney, Moscow, Warsaw and Kiev.
